One change: raw input gradients

g_i=(\partial\mu_i(\widetilde s_b)/\partial\widetilde s_b)_{b=1}^{P}
z_i^{\mathrm{normalized}}=g_i/\sqrt{\|g_i\|^2+\varepsilon_g},\qquad z_i^{\mathrm{raw}}=g_i
d_{ij}=\|z_i-\operatorname{sg}(z_j)\|^2,\qquad h_j=\operatorname{sg}\!\left(\max\{\operatorname{median}_{i}d_{ij}/\log H,\varepsilon_h\}\right)
L_1=L_{\mathrm{fit}}+\lambda\sum_i\log\!\left[\sum_j\exp(-d_{ij}/h_j)\right]

The complete 1D gradient field remains one particle. The raw variant retains gradient magnitude. Bandwidth estimation, stop-gradient references, self terms, likelihood, input preprocessing, random-point sampling, and Bayesian stage two retain their matched normalized settings. Random points redraw each optimizer step and exclude all training inputs; combined uses B training plus B random inputs.
